glosses: To cause something to fall down by shaking it, or something it is attached to.

examples.text: shake down apples from an apple tree.

glosses: To shake someone so money falls from their pockets.
To extort money from (someone) by means of threats.

examples.text: He left after shaking her down for four bits for carrying the bags.
At 58.9K, he'd be handing over practically nine thousand dollars a year to California and to the county for the privilege of being shaken down by these thicknecks.

glosses: To search exhaustively.
To subject something to a shakedown test.

translations.source_sense_description: den Fall von etwas durch Schütteln bewirken

glosses: To remove (something attached to, on or clinging to an object) by shaking.

examples.text: The archaeologists shook off the dust that had fallen from the roof, and promptly continued their work.

glosses: To dissociate oneself from (an allegation or rumour).

examples.text: Dozens of foreigners have been jailed for child sex crimes or deported to face trial in their home countries since Cambodia launched an anti-pedophilia push in 2003, to try to shake off its reputation as a haven for sex predators.

The 21st century's spectacular reimagined transport hub "set out to shake off the old image of stations. I think it's successfully done that, and it's great that others are following suit," Spinks continues.

glosses: To lose someone who is tracking you.

examples.text: The police are chasing us! Quick, turn into that side street! We've got to shake them off.

glosses: To rid oneself of a malady or its symptoms

examples.text: I just can't shake off this cold.
